articles.title: Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT
articles.summary:
GitHub’s annual month-long game jam is back for its 14th year! This November, make a game inspired by the theme SHIFT. Change gears, swap perspectives, bend reality, or just press a certain key.
Game Off, GitHub’s annual month-long game jam, returns for its 14th year this November. Thousands of developers have joined us over the years to make everything from polished platformers to wonderfully weird experiments.
Whether you’re making your first game or your fiftieth, we’d love for you to join us.
The theme for Game Off 2026 is SHIFT!
Shift gears. Shift perspectives. Shift dimensions. Shift bits. Work the night shift. Or make a game where the only buttons are the Shift keys.
How you interpret the theme is entirely up to you.
You have until December 1, 2026, at 13:37 PST to build and submit a game inspired by SHIFT. Strong or loose inspirations apply!
A one-button (or two-button) game where the Shift keys are is your only control.
A racing game where shifting gears changes more than your speed. Second gear reverses gravity, third slows time, and fourth removes the brakes.
A perspective puzzler where rotating the camera turns walls into floors and shifts shadows into platforms.
A puzzle-platformer where you shift between two overlapping realities. That broken bridge might exist in the other world. Unfortunately, so might the monster standing on it.

articles.title: Can Human Gatekeepers Keep Up With AI Generated Science?
articles.summary:
A recent scroll through social media got me thinking about trust. About half my feed was filled with AI slop that astute users would call out as being machine-generated, often to the embarrassment of the rube who unknowingly spread it and sometimes to the delight of the poster who shared it deliberately because they found it amusing or useful for sowing confusion.
Remember the good old days of GPT-3 when we could ask the chatbot anything and it would almost instantly and very confidently spit back a plausible but false answer? That’s when the word “hallucination” as applied to AI answers entered the lexicon. Six years and several versions of a few different chatbots later, I still can’t trust the answers I get, even though Claude or Gemini often do useful work for me. That’s the thing about current AI: Trust but verify. And verify you must.
Apply that maxim at scale to maintain the integrity of the scientific record and you get an idea of the challenge facing publishers of peer-reviewed scholarship. In “I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper,” freelance writer and doctor of applied mathematics Benjamin Skuse tells the story of the human gatekeepers trying to beat back the rising tide of AI slop by attempting to get his own AI-generated papers past IEEE’s defenses.
“He basically hit ‘run experiment’ and ‘write paper.’ And then he didn’t do a damn thing to it.” —Eliza Strickland

articles.title: Câncer de pulmão: comprimido diário mantém doença avançada controlada por 7 anos
articles.summary:
Um comprimido tomado uma vez ao dia conseguiu manter o câncer de pulmão avançado sob controle por sete anos em mais da metade dos pacientes que participaram de um estudo clínico. O resultado, considerado inédito para a doença, foi obtido com o lorlatinibe, medicamento desenvolvido para combater tumores que apresentam alteração genética específica.
Publicado em setembro de 2026 na revista científica Annals of Oncology, o estudo é atualização de sete anos do ensaio clínico de fase 3 CROWN. Os resultados mostram que 55% dos pacientes tratados com lorlatinibe permaneceram vivos e sem progressão da doença após esse período.
O levantamento acompanhou 296 pessoas com câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células avançado e positivo para a alteração genética ALK. Desse total, 149 receberam lorlatinibe e 147 foram tratadas com crizotinibe, outro medicamento utilizado contra esse subtipo de tumor.
No grupo que recebeu o tratamento mais recente, a mediana de sobrevida livre de progressão ainda não havia sido alcançada após sete anos de acompanhamento. Já entre os pacientes tratados com crizotinibe, esse indicador foi de apenas 9,1 meses. A probabilidade de permanecer vivo e sem progressão da doença após sete anos foi de 3% nesse segundo grupo.
Os pesquisadores também calcularam redução de 81% no risco de progressão da doença ou morte entre os pacientes que receberam lorlatinibe, na comparação com o crizotinibe.
O resultado representa avanço importante no tratamento do câncer de pulmão avança…

articles.title: NVIDIA Updates Rubin GPU Specs as First Production Hardware Arrives
articles.summary:
As we roll into the fourth quarter of 2026, NVIDIA and its partners are in the middle of the Vera Rubin ramp-up, including hyperscalers making some of the first NVL72 systems generally available to their customers. With Vera Rubin reaching the tipping point of its production roll-out, NVIDIA is also finally locking down the hardware shipping specifications. As it turns out, the company has quietly revised those specifications, with the Rubin GPU now offering less memory and scale-up networking (NVLink) bandwidth than NVIDIA previously promoted, but more scale-out bandwidth.
As initially spotted by IT Home, back in September NVIDIA posted the updated specifications for its Rubin GPU and various Rubin-based products on their webpages and in NVIDIA’s architecture datasheet. To be sure, it is not unusual for server hardware specifications to change before a product’s launch, especially for something like Vera Rubin, which was announced nearly a year in advance. NVIDIA’s case is no different, with the company previously noting that those specifications were preliminary and that “all values are up to and subject to change” at the time.
Rubin GPU: Less HBM4 Bandwidth, Less NVLink Bandwidth, More Scale-Out Bandwidth

articles.title: Northstar Security Exits Stealth With $7M to Expose Toxic Risk Combinations
articles.summary:
Northstar Security, a startup developing AI agents for security teams, has emerged from stealth mode with $7 million in seed funding.
Wing Venture Capital led the round. MVP, Outliers, and cybersecurity veterans Gerhard Eschelbeck, Renaud Deraison, and Justin Somaini also invested.
The company ingests data from existing security and IT tools to build what it calls a Security Context Graph. Updated in real time, the graph shows how identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems connect to one another.
Northstar aims to catch so-called toxic combinations. Issues such as a vulnerability, an unmanaged device, or an account with excessive privileges may seem under control on their own, but together they can expose critical business systems.
For instance, the platform could flag a laptop lacking endpoint protection whose owner is a privileged user able to reach a critical payroll system.
Analysts can investigate findings like this by asking questions in plain language. Northstar’s agents can then kick off fixes, such as installing endpoint protection, notifying the user, or limiting their access, and people can supervise those actions where appropriate.
Customers can also give external AI agents access to the graph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) and build their own security workflows. Northstar says it connects to more than 70 enterprise security and IT products, among them Okta, GitHub, Workday, Microsoft Defender and Entra, AWS, and Google Cloud.

articles.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
articles.summary:
Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20–21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise.
The attacks targeted CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw, repeatedly crashing GitLab processes, with some attempts coming close to succeeding.
Although Alpine Linux found no evidence that attackers executed code or tampered with its software packages and releases, it could not rule out a successful compromise due to missing logs and a lack of outbound connection records.
"Because we cannot rule out code execution, and the evidence we would need to confirm it no longer exists, we took the harder route and rebuilt the GitLab instance from scratch," explained the Alpine Linux team.
Alpine Linux is a small, lightweight operating system widely used as the foundation for Docker container images that run applications and services.
Their GitLab instance hosts development repositories, code reviews, and CI jobs, including the "aports" build recipes used to produce Alpine’s software packages.
That makes it a valuable supply chain target, as tampering with their GitLab environment could affect downstream software.

articles.title: Niger-based Likita Care wins 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Niger-based medical monitoring startup Likita Care has won the 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation, taking home GBP50,000 (US$67,000).
Delivered by the Royal Academy of Engineering, the Africa Prize is the continent’s biggest engineering prize. Finalists were selected from a cohort of 16 entrepreneurs who completed an eight-month training and mentoring programme.
Founded by Mamane Kabirou Ousseini, the first engineer from Niger to participate in and win the prize, Likita Care builds locally manufactured monitoring devices that can be maintained and repaired in Niger, addressing the frequent breakdown of imported equipment in resource-limited hospitals.
The platform combines connected hardware, clinical software and an AI module that interprets vital signs in real time, supporting patient, cardiac and prenatal monitoring. More than 70 units have been deployed across five medical centres in Niger.
“Winning the Africa Prize is a dream come true,” said Ousseini. The startup will use the funding to commercialise in Niger and prepare for expansion into neighbouring West African markets.
Three runners-up each received GBP10,000 (US$13,500 – South Africa’s Pee-Cycling, a urine-to-fertiliser recovery system; Kenya’s MoyoECG, a portable heart monitor; and Kenya’s Renal Roads, a mobile dialysis clinic. Ghana’s Fusion Wind Turbine won the GBP5,000 (US$6,500) One-to-Watch Award.

articles.title: FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers
articles.summary:
The FBI has confirmed that North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor were behind the $6.3 billion crypto-theft attack on Binance, making it the largest cryptocurrency heist on record.
In a security alert published Saturday, the agency attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38, linked to numerous cryptocurrency thefts.
"The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026," the FBI said.
This official attribution follows blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis, which had already linked the theft to TraderTraitor.
As previously reported, Binance linked the breach to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed the attackers to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
The attackers stole approximately $6.36 billion in cryptocurrency across ten blockchains, with most of the funds transferred in just 20 minutes.
The FBI says it has observed TraderTraitor converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH), which it expects will be further laundered through decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and instant cryptocurrency swap services.

articles.title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what has been described as a "highly sophisticated infection chain" targeting government organizations in Asia.
The activity, detailed by Kaspersky this week, targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia and involves the deployment of a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework codenamed NetamLoader.
The attack has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. Nor is it clear if the intrusion compromised more than one system and allowed the hackers to steal any sensitive information.
The Russian cybersecurity company said the artifact was detected in the first half of 2026, packaged inside a Windows cabinet archive (CAB) file placed in a directory that stores Windows operating system update packages.
It's suspected the operation involved a supply chain attack, in which bad actors compromised a trusted third-party vendor to gain access to downstream users who rely on its services or software.
The sample in question features a ".config" file that employs AppDomainManager injection to load arbitrary .NET assemblies. AppDomainManager injection is an adversarial technique used to load arbitrary payloads by hijacking .NET Framework's AppDomainManager mechanism when a .NET application starts.

articles.title: A step-by-step guide for how to kill the line-by-line code review
articles.summary:
A step-by-step guide for how to kill the line-by-line code review
Agents verify; people decide. Most teams running AI code review today have it the other way around. They point a model at the diff, ask it whether the change is good, and leave a human to skim the result and click approve.
The model reads every line, never gets tired, and holds the same standard on every PR. What it doesn’t have is your codebase’s standards. It doesn’t know them, and no matter how well you instruct it, it doesn’t always follow the ones you write down.
“Judgment needs intent, and accountability needs a person.”
It never saw what was decided, has no context for previous decisions, can’t tell you not to build the thing, and can’t be held accountable. A diff can’t give it any of that. Judgment needs intent, and accountability needs a person.
So what does a code review look like when verification goes to agents and judgment stays with people? At Aviator, we’ve been building that review into Aviator Verify. Below are its seven parts, in order.
The anatomy of an intent-driven review
Every change gets checked against two layers. Acceptance criteria describe what this change should do. Invariants are the codified rules of your engineering org or team: the standards that are always true, whatever the change.

articles.title: Europe and Canada team up in AI computing alliance that doesn't depend on Washington
articles.summary:
Sour Syrup: Geopolitical relations between Canada and the US are fraying fast, and Europe could capitalize by deepening its partnership with the proud North American nation. The new partners will likely need a lot of money, however, to make a real dent against US-based HPC powerhouses.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen recently confirmed that Canada is joining Europe's network of supercomputers, which is run by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking. Canada will become an active part of the public-private network of high-performance computing (HPC) systems, and both sides should gain something from the arrangement, at least in theory.
Von der Leyen said the new cooperation will give Canadian industry privileged access to Europe's supercomputing resources, and startups and research organizations will also be able to join in. The European Union, meanwhile, will be able to tap Canada's competitive tech industry to further expand the shared AI ecosystem.
The EuroHPC network includes 14 world-class supercomputers, 10 quantum computers, and 19 "AI factories." Its umbrella covers 67 research projects, 38 participating countries, and 36 national competence centers. EuroHPC's total budget is €8.2 billion, while a further €30 billion investment is expected to add up to seven new AI data centers, with construction starting next year.

articles.title: Wi-Fi ou câble Ethernet : pourquoi la connexion filaire garde une longueur d’avance
articles.summary:
Wi-Fi ou câble Ethernet : pourquoi la connexion filaire garde une longueur d’avance
Face à l’essor des normes sans fil toujours plus rapides, dont le Wi-Fi 7, le câble Ethernet semble dépassé. Pourtant, la liaison filaire conserve un avantage technique impossible à égaler en termes de débit.
Avec la démocratisation des box fibre ultra-modernes et la généralisation du Wi-Fi 7 dans nos foyers, tirer un fil à travers le salon pour se connecter à Internet ressemble à une pratique d’un autre âge. La tentation du tout sans-fil est ainsi très grande pour épurer son intérieur. Mais derrière ce confort indéniable se cache une réalité physique implacable : pour les usages exigeants, aucune technologie sans fil ne remplace l’efficacité directe d’un branchement Ethernet. Voici pourquoi.
Une stabilité absolue loin des obstacles et des interférences
Le principal point faible du Wi-Fi réside dans son environnement domestique. Dès que les ondes quittent la box, elles se heurtent à divers obstacles qui affaiblissent considérablement le signal jusqu’à vous si le routeur est éloigné. Alors que la bande des 2,4 GHz gère cela plutôt bien, en échange de débits plus faibles, celle des 5 GHz y est plus sensible, mais offre en contrepartie une vitesse bien supérieure.
Dans le meilleur des mondes, le sans-fil plafonne vite : comptez environ 600 à 800 Mb/s en Wi-Fi 6, autour de 1,5 Gb/s en Wi-Fi 6E, et entre 2 et 4 Gb/s en Wi-Fi 7 à proximité immédiate du routeur. Il faut ajouter à cela que vous devez …

articles.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value.
Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-based web browsers; data from Outlook profiles and Slack workspaces; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots.
"VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine," Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman said. "This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation."
To make this information more valuable, the malware uses stolen session access to search the victim's Gmail account for receipts to corroborate the home address by extracting emails related to Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal.
Once the necessary information is collected, the bundle is serialized and fed into an artificial intelligence (AI) system for analysis using OpenRouter, a unified LLM API gateway and routing service, along with a system prompt. articles.title: Digital Detox: Warum alle plötzlich wieder den iPod nutzen
articles.summary:
Digital Detox: Warum alle plötzlich wieder den iPod nutzen
Spätestens mit der Vorstellung des Widescreen-iPods mit Touch-Eingabe, des „revolutionären“ Mobiltelefons und des Internet-Communicators, waren die Zeiten des iPods vorbei. Schließlich handelt es sich dabei um das erste iPhone, das – wie Steve Jobs mehrfach wiederholte – einen iPod bereits eingebaut hatte. Heutzutage sorgt ironischerweise genau dieses Gerät dafür, dass Nutzer:innen wieder verstärkt zum iPod greifen – auch noch pünktlich zum 25-jährigen Jubiläum. Schließlich handelt es sich dabei um ein sogenanntes „Single Purpose Device“, ein Gadget, das nur einen Zweck erfüllt: ohne ständige Unterbrechung durch Nachrichten und Social Media Musik hören zu können.
Doch wie kommt heutzutage die Musik auf den iPod? Früher hat man dafür iTunes genutzt. Seit macOS Catalina handelt es sich dabei aber nur noch um einen Shop für Musik. Wir zeigen, wie du deinen alten iPod mit Bordmitteln wieder mit Musik bespielst – und welche Apps den Job noch besser erledigen.

articles.title: Open-source security in the AI exploit era: Patch without changing a thing
articles.summary:
Open-source security in the AI exploit era: Patch without changing a thing
Here’s how a vulnerability in a popular open-source library plays out in 2026: A maintainer merges a fix and publishes an advisory. Within hours, someone points a model at the diff between the old and new versions and gets a working exploit back. Your scanner flags the CVE the next morning, a ticket gets filed, and the fix is scheduled into next week’s change window. By then the exploit has been circulating for days.
That was a fine enterprise lifestyle choice last year, but it’s considered out of fashion nowadays.
And for good reason, as Michael Cembalest goes over in his “Patchmageddon” report from July 2026, which includes input from J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s cybersecurity leadership. Models such as Anthropic’s Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT–5.5 now find previously unknown vulnerabilities at a scale no human research team can match. Anthropic and its Project Glasswing partners found more than 10,000 new high- and critical-severity zero-days in the first month alone.
At the same time, the exploitation clock shrank. The note puts the median time from disclosure to first exploitation at roughly a year in 2021. Now it’s down to one day in 2026, and projected to be one minute by 2027. Almost 80% of exploitations now land on or before their public disclosure. Models can find vulnerabilities, and hackers can exploit them just as fast, if not faster.

articles.title: Agentic AI architecture demands real-time databases - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Agent demand can’t be forecast, meaning the database has to be ready for anything
Enterprises building an agentic AI architecture are learning that the database matters as much as the model. AI agents fire off thousands of unplanned queries at once — and expect answers in milliseconds.
PhoenixAI, the trade name of CelerData Inc., raised $80 million this year to develop database technology for AI agents to solve this growing problem. Established players struggle to return answers in real time, according to Ross Armstrong (pictured), senior vice president of global sales of PhoenixAI.
“There was a real gap in the market for real-time analytics, and to be able to not only ask a question but get the response back in real time was something that all the database players that are out there, even the big names in the market, couldn’t do well,” Armstrong said. “If you have customer-facing analytics or agentic AI … you need that response time to be able to meet the SLAs with your customers.”
Armstrong spoke with theCUBE’s Paul Gillin at Cloudera EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the database demands of agentic AI, real-time query performance and the need for governance and observability. (* Disclosure below.)

articles.title: The solar system may have a sixth dwarf planet, hidden against the Milky Way
articles.summary:
First look: The solar system's official roster of dwarf planets has held at five names since 2008. But a new observatory in Chile has spotted an icy world beyond Pluto that could become the sixth. It might also be the largest object found out past Neptune in about 20 years.
For now, the object announced by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory team earlier this week only goes by its provisional designation, 2026 ED138. It currently sits about 46 astronomical units from the Sun. Pluto, by comparison, averages around 40.
Nobody has measured its size directly yet. Instead, astronomers worked backward from how bright it looks at that distance, plus an estimate of how reflective its surface is, to arrive at somewhere between 600 and 1,500 km across. Even the middle of that range sits close to Ceres, the smallest dwarf planet on the official list. Rubin's solar system lead Mario Jurić put it at roughly 1,000 km and called it a once-in-a-generation kind of find.
It stayed hidden this long mostly because of where it sits in the sky. From Earth, ED138 lines up close to the plane of the Milky Way, where it's just one more faint dot against millions of background stars.
But Rubin photographs the whole southern sky every few nights with the largest digital camera ever built for astronomy, so the same dot keeps turning up in a slightly different spot. Nigeria’s technology market is usually described by its problems, from unreliable infrastructure to a volatile economy. Dotun Daniel Adekunle, OPay’s chief operating officer and chief technology officer, argues that the country’s most durable companies are the ones built to survive its worst days.
“Stubbornness is a business model in Africa,” Adekunle said in a keynote titled “Markets That Refuse to Break” at Moonshot by TechCabal on 28 October. A market this hard, he argued, rewards companies that keep adapting to local conditions.
On 9 October, OPay filed to list on the New York Stock Exchange. The filing shows revenue of $467.1 million in the first half of 2026, up from $197.5 million a year earlier, with lending overtaking payments as its largest business. Nigeria supplied 89.5% of that revenue, and the filing lists credit risk and regulation among the main threats to the business.
Adekunle pointed to the 2023 cash crunch as an example. When the naira redesign left Nigerians short of cash, transfers surged and bank apps buckled under the load. The number of payments on the NIBSS Instant Payment system jumped 45.5% in February 2023, while their total value fell 5.12%, as Nigerians moved small, everyday spending onto transfers. OPay, Adekunle said, held up because of its nationwide agent network.
“You have to adapt to the local environment, or you’ll die,” he said. “Technology is designed for the local reality.”

articles.title: FBI Links North Korea's TraderTraitor to Record $6.43 Billion Binance Crypto Heist

The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has officially attributed the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance to TraderTraitor, a North Korea-aligned elite hacking group also tracked as Jade Sleet, Pressure Chollima, PUKCHONG, Slow Pisces, and UNC4899.
The FBI, along with the U.S. Secret Service (USSS) and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), said it observed the threat actor converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH).
"It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages," the FBI said in a statement.
The agency has also provided a list of wallet addresses that the attackers are said to be using to launder the stolen assets.
The development comes as Binance said it has resumed phase one of withdrawals starting today between 6 and 9 a.m. UTC after they were paused in the wake of the incident.
"Since the incident, our teams have taken precautionary measures to safeguard the platform, conducted security assessments, and worked to verify the readiness of affected services," Binance said in a statement.
"We aim to restore withdrawals progressively as we complete security and readiness checks. Deposit services remain open and are not affected by the incident."

articles.title: File Mover Express: AWS Releases Open-Source Tool for S3 File Transfers
articles.summary:
AWS has recently released File Mover Express, an open-source application under the Apache 2.0 license for transferring large files between local systems and Amazon S3. Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, it supports parallel transfers, automatic performance tuning, retries, pause and resume, and file integrity verification.
Designed to "move media to S3 at wire speed," File Mover Express supports auto-tuned parallel transfers, pause and resume, a desktop GUI, a scriptable CLI, and automatic uploads from monitored folders.
The project is primarily developed in Go for its transfer engine and TypeScript with Angular for its graphical interface. It also supports integration with AI assistants through MCP and OIDC-based authentication with identity providers. Provanshu Dey, senior solutions architect at AWS, Asbjorn Kjaer, senior software engineer at AWS, Matthew Muccio, solutions architect at AWS, and Ross Dickson, senior customer solutions manager at AWS, explain:
At the core of File Mover Express is a daemon-based transfer engine that decouples transfers from your desktop session. The daemon can run on the machine of your choice, whether that is your workstation, a server in the data center, or an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance, while you control it from a drag-and-drop graphical user interface (GUI) or a scriptable command line interface (CLI) over an encrypted, password-protected connection.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy recently said that AWS’s large committed cloud capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with a good chunk of 2028 already allocated, while the company continues to reserve headroom for On Demand, EC2 and Bedrock.
Jassy made the remarks in a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, reported by Reuters on October 23. AWS sells capacity assurance through On-Demand Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks for ML, where a customer reserves instances in a named Availability Zone, and in the Capacity Blocks case, for a fixed window beginning on a future date. As previously reported on InfoQ, AWS raised Capacity Blocks for ML rates by about 15% uniformly across every region in January, covering P5en, P5e, P5 and P4d GPU instances along with Trn2 and Trn1.
Capacity for 2026 is already gone, Jassy said, and the company could invest well beyond the roughly $220 billion in capital expenditure planned for this year without it being a poor use of capital. On the allocation itself:

articles.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script
articles.summary:
Malicious code on the website of prediction market Polymarket sold some signed-in traders' positions and moved their funds to the hackers on October 29. The code had replaced a page-speed script that the site loaded from an outside company.
Polymarket says it is refunding about $2.7 million to 726 affected wallets. Blockchain records show crypto worth about $2.64 million reached the hackers' wallet in under an hour.
The replaced script came from DebugBear, whose real user monitoring (RUM) tool measures how fast web pages load for real visitors.
Researchers at Hudson Rock downloaded the malicious file on October 29 from the address Polymarket's site used to load the DebugBear script. They also found a change in Polymarket's site code that removed the DebugBear script.
DebugBear's DNS records were compromised through its domain registrar, the company said on X. Its early findings indicate the attack targeted one customer's website. It has seen no sign of a break-in to its own systems, though it is still looking.
Researchers at Ohey found a different server answering for DebugBear's web addresses at 18:13 UTC, when the malicious file was still online. Earlier that day, the normal script had been served from Google Cloud Storage. Each DebugBear customer loads its own copy of the script, and the file that was swapped was Polymarket's.

Intel's current entry-level N-series chips also skip performance cores, and Moon Lake would bring that approach to the company's newer tile-based design. If the leak holds, it would be the next generation of the N-series processors found in many budget machines. Intel has not confirmed the specs.

The table also suggests Moon Lake will share its layout with Wildcat Lake, the Core Series 3 processor family Intel launched in April. Wildcat Lake pairs up to two performance cores with four LP-E cores, which sit in their own low-power island on the compute tile.
Moon Lake appears to drop the performance cores and keep the island. It reportedly retains the compute tile, the multi-tile design and Wildcat Lake's BGA1516 package, and the cores are said to be Darkmont LP-E designs, the same type used in Wildcat Lake's low-power island.

articles.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
articles.summary:
A critical flaw in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud let an attacker log in as a trusted client without holding that client's private key. To do it, the attacker had to reach their HTTPS API over the network and have the trusted client's public certificate.
Once in, the attacker would act as that client, with access to the cluster and its virtual machines. If the impersonated account is privileged, the attacker could gain "root access to the host machine," Canonical said.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-112816, carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and Canonical has released fixed versions of both products.
How the Flaw Works
LXD and MicroCloud let remote clients access their APIs over mutual TLS, a setup in which the client presents a certificate to prove who it is. A client is trusted when its certificate is in the server's trust store, the list of identities the server will accept.
The flaw was in how the server checked that certificate. It compared every certificate the client sent against the trust store, but a TLS connection only proves the client owns the private key for the first certificate in the chain, the leaf. The rest of the chain is whatever the client chose to attach.
So an attacker could take a trusted client's public certificate, which is not secret, attach it to the chain behind their own, and the server would accept them as that client.

Los dispositivos eran un Q1 de 1972 y un Q1 Lite, dos máquinas de las que apenas se conservan ejemplares conocidos. Dos ordenadores que hicieron historia mucho antes de Apple
Para ponerlo en perspectiva, el Q1 original se empezó a fabricar en diciembre de 1972, 4 años antes de la aparición del Apple I. Contaba con un microprocesador Intel 8008 de 8 bits y reunía pantalla, teclado e impresora en una misma estructura, una serie de características que lo convirtieron en uno de los primeros ordenadores de sobremesa integrados.

articles.title: Exclusive: Here’s what 'renoa' — the first new fiber in 25 years — feels like | TechCrunch

Sometimes it seems like everyone — and every occasion — demands cashmere these days.
Numerous brands sell cashmere sweaters, from Bruno Cucinelli’s $7,900 cable knit cardigan to Quince’s $50 crewneck. Menswear company Loro Piana has made cashmere a cornerstone of its lineup, helping to drive the LVMH division’s valuation above €11 billion. There are even cashmere running shirts.
But as cashmere has spread throughout the fashion industry, it’s not for everyone. It’s still relatively expensive, hard to care for, and environmental fraught. The goats that produce cashmere have been trashing rangelands across Central Asia.
That may change, though. I recently experienced an alternative fiber called renoa, developed by a startup called Everbloom, that’s washable and promises to be more affordable. It could bring the cashmere experience, via a substitute material, to more products and people.
Renoa is made from sources of waste protein, including cashmere and wool scraps as well as down and feather “lint” leftover from the bedding industry. Un equipo de investigadores de la Universidad de Sheffield ha logrado reproducir por primera vez el vidrio dicroico, un curioso material de origen romano que cambia de color según cómo le dé la luz. La única pieza completa que se conserva de este material es la copa de Licurgo, del siglo IV después de Cristo. A pesar de su antigüedad, su ubicación desde entonces hasta el siglo XIX han sido todo un misterio. En cuanto a la forma de obtener el vidrio, comenzaron a encontrarse algunas pistas en la década de 1990, pero no se ha encontrado la receta definitiva hasta que los científicos de Sheffield se pusieron manos a la obra.
Oro y plata. Durante el siglo XX, varios expertos estuvieron estudiando la copa de Licurgo y concluyeron que, posiblemente, el vidrio dicroico se obtenía mezclando partículas de oro y plata. Sin embargo, ninguna de las pruebas que se hicieron dio buen resultado. Los científicos de la Universidad de Sheffield decidieron usar también esta técnica, pero con algunas modificaciones. Partieron de una reproducción de vidrio romano clásico y añadieron nanopartículas de oro y plata. Probaron distintas conformaciones con diferentes niveles de oxígeno y tiempo de horneado y, finalmente, lograron obtener un vidrio igual que el de la copa de Licurgo. Es decir, verde a la luz directa sobre su superficie y rojizo cuando se ilumina por detrás.

articles.title: Building Obsolescence-Resilient Product Lifecycles - EE Times

Artificial intelligence is reshaping the semiconductor industry, and the effects reach well beyond the data center. As memory manufacturers prioritize capacity and investment for AI-driven products, some DDR3 and DDR4 devices used in long-life systems are facing reduced availability and earlier end-of-life announcements than many designers expected. For engineers building products expected to operate for decades, semiconductor obsolescence is not just a procurement challenge. It is a fundamental design, qualification, and lifecycle-management issue.
Aerospace, defense, transportation, industrial, and medical systems are often designed around long service lives, while the semiconductor technologies within them may have significantly shorter commercial lifespans. When a critical component reaches end-of-life (EOL), engineers may face difficult choices: secure sufficient inventory, redesign the system around a replacement device, or maintain the original design.
Obsolescence cannot always be avoided, but its impact can be better managed when lifecycle considerations are built into the design and program planning process from the outset.
Understanding the lifecycle challenge
The semiconductor industry runs on technology cycles far shorter than the working lives of the systems that use its devices. A component can remain technically ideal for an application long after it stops being commercially attractive to its original manufacturer.

Tudo começa às 11h24 (pelo horário de Brasília), com a conjunção entre Lua e Marte, que não poderá ser observada devido à claridade do dia. De acordo com o guia de observação InTheSky.org, eles já poderão ser vistos bem próximos um do outro no céu da madrugada, surgindo à 1h09 e atingindo uma altitude de 40° acima do horizonte nordeste, antes de desaparecer de vista ao amanhecer, pouco antes das 5h da manhã.

articles.summary:
Voyager 1 probe to hit historic one light-day distance from Earth in 17 days — 49-year-old spacecraft travels 16 billion miles and survives nearly ten times the length of its original five-year mission
That's quite an achievement.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft, which was designed for a five-year mission to observe Jupiter and Saturn, is about to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth after nearly 50 years in flight. According to NASA, the space probe will get to that marker on Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST, making it the most distant artificial object in history. The agency has now posted a countdown clock to mark the historic moment it becomes the first human-made object to reach that distance.
One light-day isn’t a span of time, but the distance it takes for light to travel in 24 hours. Since light travels at around 186,282 miles per second or 300,000 km per second, that’s a distance of about 16 billion miles or 26 billion kilometers. By comparison, the Moon is 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) from Earth, while our planet is 93 million miles (149.6 million kilometers) from the Sun.
Voyager 1’s estimated speed in relation to the Sun is 37,844.49 mph, which makes it pretty fast (but still not the fastest human-made object ever built — the Parker Solar Probe’s holds the record at 394,736 mph). Despite that, it will still take the spacecraft 49 years, 2 months, and 13 days to get to one light-day from Earth.

articles.title: Desde una mansión hasta un castillo de 196 años: el imperio inmobiliario de Mark Zuckerberg, CEO de Meta

Su adquisición más reciente, concretada en agosto, es una propiedad de 440 acres en el condado de Waterford, Irlanda, que incluye un castillo de 196 años de antigüedad. La operación, según trascendió, le costó 51,17 millones de euros, unos 57,1 millones de dólares.
El tesoro de Zuckerberg en Florida
La adquisición de mayor valor del cofundador de Meta no fue la irlandesa, sino una realizada a principios de este año en Florida. articles.title: [Weekly funding roundup Oct 24-30] VC inflow continues to remain modest
articles.summary:
[Weekly funding roundup Oct 24-30] VC inflow continues to remain modest
The inflow of venture capital into Indian startups remained lukewarm for the month of October and this trend was reflected in the last week also.
Venture capital funding into Indian startups remained subdued in October, primarily due to the absence of large-value deals.
There was not a single deal worth more than $100 million during the month, while weekly funding remained below $200 million.
The last week of October saw total funding of $115 million across 29 deals, compared with $96 million in VC inflows during the previous week.
The largest deal of the week was a $15 million investment in healthtech startup Cent. Despite 29 transactions during the week, large-value deals remained absent.
Interestingly, two of the deals involved pure-play AI startups, a number that is expected to grow in the coming months.
As the year draws to a close, venture capital inflows into Indian startups are unlikely to differ significantly from 2025 levels. This underscores the challenges the ecosystem continues to face in attracting large volumes of capital, partly due to the lack of a strong AI investment story in the country.
The expectation is that 2027 could bring a turnaround.
Key transactions
Healthtech startup Cent raised $15 million from Blume Ventures, South Park Commons, and angel investors.

articles.title: A fully playable version of Portal prequel F-Stop leaked
articles.summary:
Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop. Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August. That didn’t include the game’s source code or map data, but those final pieces apparently hit the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together.
A fully playable version of Portal prequel F-Stop leaked
Nearly 20 years after it was canceled, the camera-based Portal prequel F-Stop is no longer lost media.
Some dialog and elements of F-Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2. But it differs dramatically from the mainline Portal games in that it’s built around a camera mechanic that lets you capture an item by taking its picture and place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid-like photos. It’s not unlike Viewfinder in that way.
The game is short, with videos showing off its full campaign all clocking in at under an hour. That’s not terribly surprising, though. F-Stop was developed as part of the “Directed Design Experiments,” a three-month period in 2007 when Valve broke into five teams to build new video game experiments.

“Our commitment remains unchanged: Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds,” the company added. “These losses will not be passed on to users.”
As for the withdrawal freeze, Binance said it did not make the decision lightly, as it understands “how important reliable access to withdrawals is for our users.” Nonetheless, the company said this was a necessary “precaution while our teams worked to contain the incident loss, assess its impact, restore affected services, and complete security checks.”
Binance will resume supporting withdrawals in phases, depending on network and asset type. As of Sunday morning, the company’s network status page showed a mix of normal, partially suspended, and fully suspended statuses — for example, Bitcoin withdrawals and deposits are still listed as partially suspended, while Ethereum deposits are normal and withdrawals are partially suspended.

Les ingénieurs de Google ont demandé un haïku au modèle d’IA Gemma 4, installé dans leur satellite expérimental, et récupéré sa réponse quand l’engin survolait le Svalbard, en Norvège. Avec ces trois vers, l’entreprise vérifie que ses puces d’IA fonctionnent en orbite, là où elle espère installer un jour des centres de données alimentés par le Soleil.
Le satellite de la taille d’un réfrigérateur lancé le 1er octobre par une fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX est le premier prototype de Suncatcher. Pour éviter la surchauffe, ses ingénieurs ne font tourner ces puces que quinze minutes d’affilée. Travis Beals, directeur de l’équipe de recherche Paradigms of Intelligence chez Google, salue dans ce haïku « la toute première réponse d’IA produite en orbite par une puce de centre de données ».
Un haïku, des poèmes et un bulletin technique écrits par Gemma 4

articles.title: Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d'internautes pendant 10 ans
articles.summary:
Des chercheurs de l’entreprise de cybersécurité Socket ont identifié un réseau de 319 extensions Chrome qui détournent les recherches des internautes. Ce système serait actif depuis dix ans et aurait potentiellement touché 13,4 millions d’utilisateurs.
Des extensions Chrome destinées à enregistrer vos requêtes
De prime abord, ces extensions Chrome, destinées à détourner les recherches des internautes, semblent inoffensives en se présentant comme des convertisseurs de DFD, des outils de recherche de manuels, des moteurs de recherche sécurisés ou encore des assistants IA de recherche. Mais en réalité, elles ont un double objectif. D’une part, les requêtes saisies dans Chrome transitent sur des serveurs proxy contrôlés par les opérateurs des extensions. D’autre part, ces extensions redirigent l’internaute vers Yahoo ou Bing afin que les pirates bénéficient de commissions de parrainage, étant donné que du trafic est généré sur ces deux moteurs de recherche concurrents de Google.
Pour être plus précis, les pirates exploitent un paramètre de Chrome qui permet à une extension de remplacer le moteur de recherche par défaut. Par ailleurs, il faut noter que certaines de ces extensions ne demandent aucune autorisation particulière de la part de l’internaute.
Comment éviter tout risque ?
Ces extensions malveillantes représentent un problème principalement à deux niveaux. Le premier, le moins grave : les pirates se font de l’argent sur le dos des internautes en les redirigeant vers Yahoo …

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView could add security camera features
articles.summary:
Reddit user pdfu found hints hidden in the HomeView 27.2 code that Apple could be adding security camera features to its smart home hub. The strings describe a security camera mode with motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, as well as privacy functions. According to pdfu, there is a setup page that even explicitly reads: “Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video.”
Apple’s HomeView could add security camera features
Code strings in HomeView’s software suggest Apple could launch a Secure Video feature soon.
Supposedly, the video feeds will only be visible to members of the home, and will both show an indicator light and play a sound when either someone is watching the camera feed or when it starts to record. Home members will also get a notification anytime settings are changed for the Secure Video mode. It will also include customizable options for what to detect, stream, or record, based on whether you’re home, away, or asleep.
Some wondered why Apple did not allow HomeView to double as a security camera at launch, and the company hasn’t said anything to suggest the features are coming. But, considering how central privacy is to Apple’s marketing, the company may be waiting to fine-tune those features before launch.

articles.title: KI-Bilder: So schaffst du endlich konsistente Charaktere

Die Kosten summieren sich. Wer professionelle KI-Werkzeuge nutzen will, landet monatlich schnell bei dreistelligen Abo-Beträgen. Nutzer:innen balancieren zwischen Qualitätsanspruch und der Notwendigkeit, Budget und Nerven zu schonen. Workflow-Tools nach dem Bausteinprinzip können mit diesem unübersichtlichen Prozess Schluss machen.
Visuelles Arbeiten für KI-Bilder und -Videos
In klassischen KI-Tools arbeiten Nutzer:innen meist linear: Ein Input führt zu einem Ergebnis, das sie in den nächsten Arbeitsschritt mitnehmen. Stimmt am Ende ein Detail nicht, beginnt der Prozess von vorn. Der Baustein-Ansatz aktueller Tools wie Flora oder Magnific Spaces dreht das Prinzip um: Die Arbeit lebt nicht in Chats, sondern auf einer Arbeitsfläche.
Den Anfang macht die Idee. Textbausteine auf Basis kleiner KI-Assistenten machen daraus einen verbesserten Bildprompt, und von dort führt per Drag-and-drop eine Verbindung zu einem Modul für Bildgenerierung – oder gleich zu mehreren Modulen, die unterschiedliche KI-Modelle nutzen. Den Prompt könnt ihr durch Referenzbilder als Kontext ergänzen. Jedes Bild kann in demselben Baustein neu generiert werden, ohne vorherige Versionen zu verlieren, bevor ihr im nächsten Baustein etwa Perspektive oder Beleuchtung ändert. Auch LLMs, Upscaler und andere Tools sind so ansprechbar, ebenso wie verschiedene Videomodelle, die das Standbild mit einem entsprechenden Prompt in Bewegung bringen.

articles.title: Ese kebab después de una noche de fiesta no es casualidad: el alcohol cambia tus ganas de comer
articles.summary:
Es fácil haber escuchado en alguna ocasión que el alcohol tiene "calorías vacías" puesto que solo nos engorda sin aportarnos nada más, pero la realidad es que esto solo es una pequeña parte de la mala nutrición dietética que hay detrás. Y es que, al consumir alcohol, estamos desencadenando una compleja cascada neuroendocrina que altera radicalmente nuestras preferencias alimentarias, haciendo que prefiramos comida mucho más calórica y ultraprocesada que la más sana.
Efecto aperitivo. Los estudios que hay ahora mismo publicados apuntan a que hay un patrón bastante claro que relaciona la ingesta de alcohol con nuestros hábitos alimentarios, y que puede justificar el clásico kebab que se toma la gente después de una noche de fiesta.
Por ejemplo, un estudio publicado en 2015 demostró que una dosis de 20 gramos de alcohol aumentaba la ingesta de comida en 11%. Pero lo más interesante de todo es que el alcohol elevaba sobre todo el deseo por los alimentos salados y con mucha grasa, mientras que reducía las ganas de tomar algo dulce.
Nos estimula diferentes sentidos, como el del olfato, puesto que sabemos que una precarga de alcohol potencia la respuesta del hipotálamo ante los olores de comida en comparación con olores de otros elementos. Esto hace que pasear por la calle con alguna copa de más pueda hacer que estemos más tentados de entrar en algún establecimiento de comida.

articles.title: Lenovo's 'encrypted' fingerprint USB drive is just an unencrypted SD card in a fancy case — AI-assisted follow-up finds a backdoor and hardcoded keys in other ‘secure’ USB products
articles.summary:
Lenovo's 'encrypted' fingerprint USB drive is just an unencrypted SD card in a fancy case — AI-assisted follow-up finds a backdoor and hardcoded keys in other ‘secure’ USB products
The fingerprint only switched the USB connection on; nothing on the card was encrypted.
Security researcher Xusheng Li found that a Lenovo ThinkPlus FU100 fingerprint USB stick, sold as an AES-256-encrypted device for data security, ended up being just a plain SD card internally, HackingPassion reports. The fingerprint reader only enabled the USB connection, and nothing on the card was actually encrypted. An AI-assisted follow-up last week discovered what Li calls backdoor accounts on another maker’s drive, as well as hardcoded keys in other supposedly secure USB storage products.
The FU100 is “just an SD card in a fancy case,” Li said in a March conference talk. It is, as a result, trivial for anyone with physical access to get to the drive’s data. One of his takeaways: “‘Hardware security’ can be pure marketing.” This isn’t the first time drive makers’ own encryption has failed, and it won’t be the last.
The original ThinkPlus FU100 analysis happened last year, with an interim fix using epoxy over the card. A later fix by Lenovo, put out early this year for the FU100, FU200 and TU800 drives, as well as the TSD303 SSD, requires owners to call a China service line, then either send devices back for replacement or get an on-site firmware upgrade. Ce chiffre vient d’une seule entreprise et ne vaut pas forcément pour toutes les références de stratifié. Mais les délais, eux, s’allongent nettement. D’après les industriels interrogés par Nikkei Asia, certaines commandes de PCB demandent jusqu’à 30 mois, deux fois plus qu’il y a un an. Une carte commandée aujourd’hui pourrait donc n’arriver qu’à la fin 2028.

Il y a quelques jours, la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) a déclenché un premier essai de choc par explosion sous-marine sur la coque de l'ex-frégate anti-sous-marine Latouche-Tréville, au large de Saint-Mandrier-sur-Mer, dans le Var. Une frégate à la retraite reprend du service… comme cobaye

Hubble is in no immediate danger of burning up in the Earth’s atmosphere, but its time will run out in the early to mid 2030s unless its orbit is boosted. So NASA is taking proposals from the private sector to see if anyone can save it.
NASA hopes the commercial space industry can help save Hubble
The Hubble Space Telescope will come crashing to Earth sometime in the 2030s without a boost.
In a post on NASA’s site, Administrator Jared Isaacman said:
“Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible … If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble’s life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe.”

articles.title: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’ | TechCrunch

Data centers are deeply unpopular. But what if we called them something else?
Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too.
The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “the issue” in the presidential election.
So OpenAI is to influence the AI debate moving forward, with Lehane discussing several proposals, including the development of AI “speed limits”; finding ways to help people see AI as empowering them in their daily lives; pushing the U.S. to take a role in developing global standards — and yes, rebranding data centers as “AI compute campuses.”
Lehane also described the conversation around data centers (a debate that has pushed Amazon and Microsoft to say they will no longer use NDAs in their negotiations with local governments) as “good and healthy.”
“Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects,” he said.

Dragging the Windows Taskbar To Move It Is Dead, and That's a Feature
Microsoft recently restored the ability for Windows users to move the Taskbar to any screen edge, nearly five years after Windows 11 launched. The Windows 11 implementation, however, is not the same as it was in Windows 10, where users could click and drag to move the Taskbar and lock it in place when they were happy with its position. Instead, Windows 11 makes users go into the settings app to change the Taskbar position, and now, in response to a news story about a third-party utility that allows Taskbar dragging, Windows Vice President of Design, Diego Baca, explains that this is indeed a feature, not a bug, and that the drag-and-drop repositioning often caused accidental movements.
Diego Baca, Windows Vice President of Design at MicrosoftFrom our research, dragging the Taskbar to reposition it can lead to accidental movements, which is one of the reasons "Lock the Taskbar" existed in previous versions of Windows. We also found that changing the Taskbar position isn't something people do frequently.
We felt that providing a discoverable setting, just one right-click away, was a more intentional and predictable experience. It's a deliberate design decision, not a missing capability.

Michel Leonard est chef de projet de Space HPC, la machine que l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a installée dans son centre ESRIN (Institut européen de recherches spatiales) de Frascati, près de Rome. Quand je l’ai rencontré sur place, il m’a fait la réponse la plus simple possible : « Le calculateur sert principalement à traiter beaucoup de données et à faire beaucoup de calculs sur ces données. On a de plus en plus de données, et pour les traiter, il faut de la puissance de calcul. »
La machine a été inaugurée le 12 mars 2025, en partenariat avec l’entreprise Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE). D’après sa documentation officielle, c’est le tout premier système de calcul haute performance de l’ESA (on parle de HPC, pour High Performance Computing).
Pourquoi ce besoin aujourd’hui ? Parce que les volumes de données grossissent plus vite que ce qu’un ordinateur classique peut avaler. « Les données se multiplient de façon exponentielle, et le temps de calcul qu’on doit consacrer à leur traitement augmente de la même façon », m’explique Michel Leonard.
L’ESRIN est le centre de l’ESA dédié à l’observation de la Terre. Ses missions fournissent en continu des données satellitaires, réutilisées dans de nombreuses applications, y compris grand public. articles.title: Open-source USB tool unlocks Nvidia's half-speed GPU AI limiter on Windows — lifts GPU's FP16 math performance up to 65%, UEFI unlocker covers RTX 20, 30, and 40-series desktops and laptops
articles.summary:
Open-source USB tool unlocks Nvidia's half-speed GPU AI limiter on Windows — lifts GPU's FP16 math performance up to 65%, UEFI unlocker covers RTX 20, 30, and 40-series desktops and laptops
It runs from a USB stick before Windows loads and has to run again on every boot.
A new open-source UEFI tool boots from USB and unlocks significant extra tensor performance on RTX 20, 30, and 40-series desktop and laptop GPUs, making the half-speed AI throttle hack a whole lot easier to try on Windows. No VBIOS flash or patched driver needed: the tool runs from a FAT32 stick before the Nvidia driver loads at every boot, and then voila, the developer’s own laptop RTX 4060 hit 65% higher FP16 math.
The “UEFI pre-driver NVIDIA GPU unlocker,” or nv-uefi-unlocker project, removes Nvidia’s tensor limiter using the community V67 payload with read-back verification. This tricks Nvidia’s signed Booter firmware into opening the write lock on two speed-selector registers, allowing the tensor units to run at full rate. The unlock can now run entirely from a bootable USB drive, on Windows as well as Linux, whereas previously it worked primarily through manually installed Linux modules, with Windows support only experimental. The read-back verification part makes things safer, which was a concern with the experimental builds.

Deux téléviseurs peuvent respecter les mêmes normes colorimétriques sans que leurs images paraissent identiques à tous les spectateurs. Une étude scientifique publiée début octobre dans la revue Optics Express montre comment certaines technologies d'affichage modernes peuvent accentuer ces différences de perception.
Comme nous le détaillons dans notre protocole de tests de téléviseurs, nous accordons une attention particulière à la fidélité des couleurs. Température de couleur, Delta E, couverture des espaces colorimétriques : autant de mesures qui permettent de vérifier si un écran respecte les standards de l'industrie. Mais même avec un point blanc parfaitement réglé sur D65, deux spectateurs ne verront pas nécessairement la même chose.
C'est ce phénomène qu'ont étudié Andrew Rider et Andrew Stockman, de l'University College London (UCL), avec John Frith, dans une publication intituléeWhy the colours of modern displays can look so different to different observers. Leurs travaux s'intéressent au métamérisme d'observateur, qui prend une importance particulière avec certaines technologies d'affichage modernes.
Pourquoi les écrans modernes accentuent les différences entre nos yeux

Sur le dépôt GitHub du projet, on peut voir qu’elle puise dans environ 930 000 des articles les plus consultés de Wikipédia, des encyclopédies médicales comme WikiMed et MedlinePlus, les guides d’urgence de l’agence américaine de gestion des crises (FEMA) et des CDC, des manuels militaires de survie, mais aussi des tutoriels wikiHow et des guides de réparation iFixit.

AI-driven high-bandwidth memory demand is reshaping memory markets, boosting mature flash products as Macronix expands its portfolio for AI workloads.
The artificial intelligence (AI) boom continues to rewrite the rules of the game in the memory industry. Over the past year, major memory makers such as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron have continued shifting capacity and capital spending toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced server memory, crowding out mature and specialty products. At the same time, the growing scale of AI models and inference workloads is expanding memory requirements beyond capacity and bandwidth to data tiering, movement and processing, further reshaping the architecture of the overall memory system.
Martin Lin, director of marketing at Macronix International, said in an interview with EE Times Taiwan that the changes brought by AI are not simply about increasing memory demand, but that “the entire memory architecture is changing.” From the growing use of NOR flash in AI servers and the search for more capacity- and cost-efficient memory tiers beyond HBM, to the growing importance of key value (KV) cache in inference performance, memory is gradually evolving from a conventional data-storage component into a core element affecting AI system performance, cost and architectural design.

El proyecto, bautizado Keybytes, se distribuye como código abierto y permite que cualquier usuario reorganice las teclas en distintas configuraciones según su preferencia.
Nathan Alspaugh, estudiante de ingeniería aeroespacial, diseñó el sistema con el objetivo de resolver un problema personal: nunca quiso comprometerse con una disposición de teclado fija. Cada tecla, denominada Keybit, incorpora un microcontrolador RISC-V y pogo pins en sus cuatro costados, lo que permite la transmisión de energía y conexiones I2C entre módulos adyacentes. articles.title: Delta E : que signifie vraiment cette mesure utilisée dans nos tests de TV, vidéoprojecteurs, smartphones et PC portables ?
articles.summary:
Delta E : que signifie vraiment cette mesure utilisée dans nos tests de TV, vidéoprojecteurs, smartphones et PC portables ?
Le delta E revient régulièrement dans nos tests de téléviseurs, moniteurs et vidéoprojecteurs. Cette valeur permet d'évaluer la fidélité des couleurs affichées par un écran par rapport à une référence. Mais que signifie réellement un delta E de 1, 3 ou 5 et comment est-il mesuré ?
Le delta E est omniprésent dans nos tests de téléviseurs, moniteurs et vidéoprojecteurs, mais aussi sur les smartphones et les ordinateurs portables. Derrière cette valeur se cache une mesure colorimétrique assez complexe, qui permet d’évaluer l’écart entre une couleur affichée et celle qu’elle devrait réellement être. Voici comment elle fonctionne et, surtout, comment l’interpréter !
Lorsque nous mesurons un téléviseur ou un moniteur au laboratoire, certaines valeurs sont relativement faciles à comprendre. Une luminosité de 1000 cd/m² est supérieure à une luminosité de 500 cd/m², mais avec le delta E, les choses sont un peu moins intuitives.
Cette valeur, que nous indiquons systématiquement dans nos mesures de colorimétrie, ne représente ni une couleur, ni une luminosité, elle quantifie en fait une distance entre deux couleurs : celle que l'écran devrait afficher et celle que nous mesurons réellement.

Malgré l'interdiction théorique du démarchage téléphonique sans consentement, ces appels indésirables restent un véritable fléau au quotidien. La bonne nouvelle ? Vos meilleures armes demeurent les premiers chiffres qui s'affichent sur votre écran. Face aux appels frauduleux ou émis par des acteurs qui contournent allègrement la loi, il est heureusement possible de reprendre le contrôle : la clé réside souvent dans les premiers chiffres qui s'affichent sur votre écran.

articles.title: Hasta ahora, las apps de siempre solo podían hacer lo que sus creadores querían. La IA está dinamitando eso
articles.summary:
Antes descargabas una aplicación para algo muy concreto que necesitabas y debías aguantar el resto de funciones extra. Para competir, los desarrolladores fueron engordando sus apps hasta niveles a menudo absurdos. Así que ahí estabas tú, con una aplicación que te servía para una cosa específica y que añadía otras mil funciones que gastaban recursos en balde. El desarrollador mandaba, y la única vía de vuelta eran las sugerencias.
La dificultad de contentar a todos. Una aplicación suele despegar para cubrir una necesidad concreta. Que el usuario beba agua, que pueda activar la linterna o que comparta las fotos con sus amigos. Cuando hay decenas de aplicaciones que cubren dichas necesidades, la única forma de seguir destacando es engordar el software. Además, hay otro problema añadido: siempre habrá tareas muy específicas que se quedarán fuera porque el dev no puede especializar la aplicación a cada usuario.
Es imposible hacer feliz a todo el mundo. Como el meme que puso mi madre en el grupo de WhatsApp, lo primero es hacerse feliz a uno mismo. Si sabes justo lo que quieres, ¿por qué no tener un botón para eso en la aplicación? Es justo lo que está facilitando la IA.
Si quieres algo, hazlo tú. El vibecoding está permitiendo algo que hace unos pocos años era imposible: crear una aplicación como ese sastre que hace trajes a medida. Solo que el sastre ya no es un desarrollador, sino un LLM con una interfaz de chat.

articles.title: Nach Mega-Hack: Binance erlaubt wieder Auszahlungen
articles.summary:
Krypto-Kunden kommen mit blauem Auge davon: Binance ermöglicht nach Mega-Hack wieder Auszahlungen
Am 29. Oktober 2026 hatten laut FBI wahrscheinlich nordkoreanische Hacker:innen Digitalwährungen im Wert von 6,3 Milliarden US-Dollar von der weltgrößten Krypto-Börse Binance gestohlen. Die komplexe Attacke soll über den Laptop einer Person aus der IT-Abteilung erfolgt sein, wie Binance erklärte. Der Großteil des Diebstahls soll innerhalb eines Zeitraums von nur 20 Minuten erfolgt sein.
Auszahlung nach Hack: Erste Phase gestartet
Auch weil es Binance mit Hilfe der US-Behörden und Partnerfirmen gelungen war, rund die Hälfte der betroffenen Vermögenswerte einzufrieren, hielt sich der Schaden in Grenzen. Entsprechend verlief der Einbruch der Kurse von Bitcoin und Co weniger stark als befürchtet.
Seit dem 1. November 2026 können Binance-Kund:innen zudem wieder Auszahlungen von ihren Konten vornehmen. Allerdings ist diese Möglichkeit in einer ersten Phase auf größere Kryptowährungen wie Bitcoin, Ether und Dogecoin beschränkt.
Große Kapitalflucht bleibt zunächst aus
Wie Binance via X mitteilte, sei es in den ersten Stunden nach der Wiedereröffnung des Krypto-Handels zwar zu starken Abflüssen gekommen. Die große Kapitalflucht sei aber bisher ausgeblieben.

articles.title: Why Gulf businesses buy software and keep using paper
articles.summary:
Why Gulf businesses buy software and keep using paper
An article by Matthew Truth, Co-Founder and Product Lead at Octabiz
Walk into many small shops in Oman, and in parts of the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain too, and you will still see the notebook. A customer pays, and the sale goes on paper at that moment. Stock that arrives is written down: what came in, how much and when. At the end of the day, and again at the end of the month, someone goes through the pages and ticks everything off so nothing goes wrong.
What surprised me is how many of these same businesses have already bought software. They paid for an inventory system or a sales tool, and then they kept the notebook. The software sits there, used a little or not at all.
Across the Gulf, the money paid for a product doesn't necessarily translate into actual use. I think that gap is the real opportunity, and most of the market is looking past it.
Why paper keeps winning
Paper has three things going for it.
The first is simplicity. A pen and a page need no training.
The second is trust. What I write is right in front of me. I can see it, and I am the one who owns it.
The third is reliability. The notebook has one clear purpose. I open it, write down a purchase or a sale, and when I need something later, I flip a few pages and find it.
Software that wants to replace the notebook has to match all three. Being more powerful is not enough.
Two jobs, not one

articles.title: Anycubic and Thingiverse announce exclusive 3D printing partnership — MakerOnline platform to offer '1-click' multicolor 3MF models
articles.summary:
Anycubic and Thingiverse announce exclusive 3D printing partnership — MakerOnline platform to offer '1-click' multicolor 3MF models
Eight months after leaving UltiMaker, the world’s largest 3DP file site teams up with Anycubic.
Anycubic has announced an exclusive partnership with Thingiverse, the world’s oldest and largest repository of free STL models for 3D printing. The move comes roughly eight months after Thingiverse was purchased from UltiMaker by MyMiniFactory. This is clearly a “collaboration,” not an acquisition, as Thingiverse remains part of the MyMiniFactory family and dedicated to the SoulCrafted, human-made art movement.
Instead, Anycubic will gain permission to share the files directly with its own users on the MakerOnline platform. Selected models will be adapted for multicolor printing and converted by Anycubic from STL to 3MF format for compatible printers (such as the Kobra X), helping reduce manual setup and making it easier for users to move from choosing a model to preparing it for printing.
As Thingiverse is an open platform, this partnership aims to make it easier for Creators to have their content enjoyed by Anycubic 3D printer owners around the world, said Romain Kidd, CEO of Thingiverse, in an email to Tom’s Hardware. Kidd said the collaboration will allow Anycubic users to have close to a “1-click” printing experience.

articles.title: “Es bastante terrible”: Sam Altman sobre la cantidad de memoria RAM que se ‘desperdicia’ en computadoras personales
articles.summary:
Sam Altman, consejero delegado de OpenAI, afirmó que es “bastante terrible” que millones de personas mantengan memoria RAM en sus ordenadores domésticos sin aprovecharla al máximo, en momentos en que este componente se ha encarecido por la demanda de los centros de datos dedicados a inteligencia artificial.
Sus declaraciones, formuladas en el pódcast Cheeky Pint, plantean que la distribución actual de la DRAM (memoria dinámica de acceso aleatorio) a nivel mundial resulta ineficiente.
El argumento de la distribución global de recursos
Altman explicó su postura durante una conversación con John Collison, cofundador de Stripe, sobre si los modelos de código abierto de inteligencia artificial permitirían reducir la dependencia de la infraestructura de las grandes compañías tecnológicas. “Desde el punto de vista de la distribución global de recursos, es bastante terrible que todo el mundo tenga una parte del suministro mundial limitado de DRAM en su propio ordenador y que se utilice el 5% del tiempo”, señaló el directivo.
Para el ejecutivo, el problema radica en que la capacidad de fabricación de memoria RAM es limitada, mientras que su uso en ordenadores particulares resulta esporádico. En contraste, sostuvo que concentrar ese mismo recurso en centros de datos permitiría un aprovechamiento constante. “Lo que quieres es maximizar la utilización en la nube si estás intentando lidiar con un entorno de suministro tan limitado”, indicó Altman, según recoge el medio especializado Tom’s…

articles.title: Religiöse Gründe: Uni-Mitarbeiter verweigert KI-Einsatz
articles.summary:
Religiöse Gründe: Uni-Mitarbeiter verweigert KI-Einsatz
Der Einsatz von KI erhitzt seit Längerem die Gemüter. Die einen sorgen sich um Cybergefahren oder kritisieren den KI-bedingten Stellenabbau. Andere fragen sich, welche Auswirkungen die neue Technologie konkret auf das menschliche Denken hat. Zu ihnen gehört David Durman. Er arbeitet als Verwaltungsmitarbeiter an der University of Kentucky und bezeichnet sich selbst als Humanist. Wie Religion News berichtet, hat er jetzt eine religiös begründete Ausnahmegenehmigung erhalten, die ihn vom KI-Einsatz befreit.
KI nicht mit Humanismus vereinbar?
Immer mehr Menschen müssen sich am Arbeitsplatz mit neuen KI-Tools auseinandersetzen. Oft sollen sie Prozesse beschleunigen und so die Produktivität steigern. Als die University of Kentucky ihre Mitarbeiter:innen aufforderte, KI in ihre Arbeitsabläufe zu integrieren, machte sich Durman Sorgen. Er hatte das Gefühl, er solle sein Denken in der täglichen Arbeit an einen Chatbot auslagern. Das empfand er als Verstoß gegen seine Überzeugungen.
„Der Prozess und die Arbeit, die damit verbunden sind, Situationen zu durchdenken – im Rahmen meiner Arbeit, meiner Ethik und der Art und Weise, wie ich mit anderen Menschen umgehe – sind ein wesentlicher Bestandteil meiner Entwicklung zu einem moralischen Menschen“, erklärte er im Interview mit Religion News. „Und diese Arbeit auszulagern, unabhängig davon, ob sie anstrengend ist oder nicht, untergräbt meine Fähigkeit, moralisch zu handeln.“

articles.title: China ofrece sueldos de un millón de yuanes por el ingeniero de IA que también buscan Anthropic y OpenAI

Un millón de yuanes al año (unos 134.000 euros). Ese es el sueldo que las grandes tecnologícas chinas, entre ellas ByteDance, Tencent y Alibaba, están ofreciendo a un perfil técnico muy concreto, como explica el South China Morning Post: el forward-deployed engineer o ingeniero desplegado en cliente. O lo que es lo mismo, hablar con el cliente para entender su problema, eligen las herramientas de IA adecuadas e implementan la solución.
Un dato para contextualizar la oferta: según la Oficina Nacional de Estadística de China, en 2025 los profesionales técnicos del sector TI en empresas chinas de cierto tamaño ganaron de media 275.504 yuanes, y el conjunto de su personal, 106.080 yuanes. Es decir, entre casi 4 y 10 veces más.
Se los rifan. Un par de ejemplos conocidos: Tencent ha puesto anuncios en la plataforma Boss Zhipin buscando FDE para su división de IA. Ofrece entre 35.000 y 65.000 yuanes al mes y 15 pagas, esto es: hasta 975.000 yuanes al año. Bytedance ofrece entre 35.000 y 70.000 yuanes y también 15 pagas.
Un informe de Maimai (algo así como el LinkedIn de China) ha registrado un crecimiento en búsquedas de ese perfil de 1.523 % en los siete primeros meses del año frente al mismo periodo de 2025, lo que en la práctica convierte ese perfil técnico de IA en el que tiene más crecimiento. Mientras tanto, el Ministerio de Industria y Tecnologías de la Información ha lanzado un comunicado animando a las empresas a crear equipos FDE.

articles.title: Pourquoi payer avec son téléphone est bien plus sûr qu’utiliser sa vraie carte bancaire
articles.summary:
Pourquoi payer avec son téléphone est bien plus sûr qu’utiliser sa vraie carte bancaire
Approcher son smartphone du terminal de paiement suffit pour régler ses achats. Pourtant, le commerçant ne reçoit jamais votre véritable numéro de carte bancaire lors de l’opération. Un tour de magie en trois étapes simples.
À la caisse, dégainer son téléphone a largement remplacé le geste de sortir sa carte bancaire pour payer. Si la manœuvre semble identique au paiement sans contact d’un support plastique classique, la mécanique interne diffère totalement. Là où une CB traditionnelle transmet directement ses informations au terminal du magasin, Apple Pay et Google Pay dressent un mur infranchissable entre vos vraies coordonnées et le vendeur, pour plus de sécurité et de confidentialité.
La tokenisation : un faux numéro de carte généré pour votre smartphone
Le cœur de cette sécurité repose sur un procédé appelé “tokenisation”. Lorsque vous enregistrez votre carte bancaire sur votre téléphone, vos véritables numéros ne sont jamais stockés dans la mémoire de l’appareil. articles.title: MIT engineer releases open-source 'Keybytes' magnetic mechanical keyboard
articles.summary:
This 'truly modular' keyboard can be built like a Lego set — meaning you can add as many keys as you like
MIT student creates 'Keybytes' magnetic keyboard
- Keybytes lets users assemble custom keyboards from magnetically connected individual keys
- Every Keybit contains its own RISC-V microcontroller for individual key operation
- A full-size Keybytes configuration could cost approximately $900 to assemble
MIT student Nathan Alspaugh has developed Keybytes, an open source keyboard project that lets users create custom layouts by connecting individual keys to a central controller.
The design uses magnetic connections and dedicated microcontrollers to support flexible arrangements.
Keybytes consists of two main elements: the Keyword controller and individual Keybit modules, which connect magnetically to form a personalised keyboard.
Magnetic keys allow custom layouts
Each Keybit contains a RISC-V microcontroller, allowing individual keys to operate independently rather than relying entirely on one central processor.
Every Keybit measures 19.05 x 19.05mm, corresponding to a standard 1U keyboard unit.
Its four-sided pogo pin connections carry power and I2C communications, allowing modules to connect through different edges and accommodate varied arrangements.
The central Keyword module contains two stacked circuit boards, with an Arm Cortex M4 microcontroller.

Ce monde gelé tourne à 46 unités astronomiques du Soleil, soit 46 fois la distance entre la Terre et notre étoile, alors que Pluton s’en tient en moyenne à une quarantaine d’unités. Les autres télescopes ne voyaient en lui qu’un point faible, noyé au milieu des étoiles d’arrière-plan.
